summary.text: A 61-year-old man with end-stage kidney disease due to diabetic nephropathy received a living-unrelated donor kidney transplant from his wife 15 years ago, at age 46. Seven years after transplantation an allograft biopsy was compatible with antibody-mediated rejection, and he was treated with plasma exchange, intravenous immunoglobulin and rituximab; a later biopsy raised suspicion of chronic active rejection. At 14 years after transplantation ultrasonography showed a right hepatic lobe mass, and liver MRI confirmed hepatocellular carcinoma at segments VI and II.

Tacrolimus was reduced to a 2-4 ng/mL trough target and was steady for 2 weeks before open wedge liver resection of segments VI and II/III under the Pringle maneuver, with 600 mL blood loss. On postoperative day 1 he developed oliguria and transient liver enzyme elevation, and tacrolimus C0 was elevated at 12.6 ng/mL; on postoperative day 2 C0 rose further to 15.8 ng/mL with a new tremor in both upper extremities and tension-type headache.

The evening tacrolimus dose was withheld on postoperative day 1 and tacrolimus was stopped from postoperative days 2-5, with supportive care. Intravenous furosemide was started on day 2 and tapered off by day 4. Serum creatinine peaked at 4.98 mg/dL on day 3, when maximum total bilirubin was 5.8 mg/dL. By day 6 tacrolimus C0 was 6.8 ng/mL and a 0.5 mg evening dose was restarted.

Serum creatinine gradually returned to baseline by day 7, coinciding with normalization of tacrolimus C0 and liver function tests, and headache and tremor resolved by day 7. Transaminases were normal by day 10 and bilirubin was 2.1 mg/dL on day 12. The final diagnosis was hepatocellular carcinoma in a kidney transplant recipient with tacrolimus toxicity after wedge liver resection and transient ischemic liver injury.
